The Vifocus position

A house you no longer want should not take six more months of your life to leave.

The traditional sale asks everything of the person who can least afford it: fix the roof, clear the rooms, stage the photos, host the strangers, wait out the inspections — and then pay a commission for the privilege. That process serves the listing. It does not serve the owner.

Vifocus works the other way. One conversation, one number, explained line by line, and a closing date you choose. The property stays exactly as it is — the repairs, the tenants, the history — and becomes our problem the day it becomes ours. If a traditional listing would honestly net you more, we will tell you that on the call.

Victor Alvarez Founder — Vifocus, New York

Questions

Asked on almost every call.

Do I really not have to fix or clean anything?

Correct. As-is means as-is: leave the repairs, the clutter, even the furniture you don't want. We price the property in its current condition and handle everything after closing.

How is my offer calculated?

From three things, all shown to you on the call: what similar properties nearby have actually sold for, the cost of the repairs the property needs, and the standard costs of buying and holding it. You see the same numbers we use — if a line doesn't make sense, ask and we walk it again.

How fast can you close?

As fast as about 14 days when the title is clear — and slower whenever you need it slower. You choose the closing date, and it can move if your plans change.

Are there any fees or commissions?

No agent commissions and no listing fees — there's no agent and no listing. We also cover standard closing costs. The offer number is the number you plan around.

What if I have tenants, or I'm behind on payments?

Both are common, and neither stops a sale. Tenants can stay in place through closing, and if you're behind or facing foreclosure, a fast closing can stop the process — the sooner we talk, the more options you have.

What if the property is inherited or in probate?

We buy inherited properties regularly, including ones still moving through probate in New York or New Jersey. Tell us where things stand on the call and we'll map the timeline with you.

What if I still have a mortgage on the property?

That's the normal case, not the exception. At closing, the existing mortgage is paid off out of the sale through the title company, and the remainder goes to you. On the call we work from what you'd actually net, not just the headline number.

Am I obligated if I get an offer?

No. The call and the offer are free, with no obligation and no pressure. Plenty of owners take the number, think it over, and call back weeks later.
